enriched.title: Present Perfect e Vocabulário de Ações Comuns
enriched.summary: Esta aula aborda o uso do Present Perfect em diferentes contextos, com foco em ações já realizadas, e introduz vocabulário relacionado a ações do dia a dia. Também explora a diferença entre 'been to' e 'gone to'.

vocabulary.definition: Physical substance; that which occupies space and has mass.
examples: Matter is what makes up the physical world.

vocabulary.definition: Something that is outside or surpasses the physical substance.
examples: The concept of the soul is often considered beyond matter.

vocabulary.definition: To turn or cause to turn around quickly.
examples: She spun the globe, and pointed to Latin America.

vocabulary.definition: To shape or force something straight into a curve or angle.
examples: Light rays bend as they pass from air to water.

vocabulary.definition: To ascertain the size, amount, or degree of something.
examples: We need to measure the length of the table.

vocabulary.translation: um ao outro, um do outro
vocabulary.definition: Used to show a reciprocal action or relationship.
examples: The two companies are in competition with each other.

vocabulary.definition: Unable to think clearly or understand something.
examples: My grandpa gets very confused sometimes.

grammar.explanation: The Present Perfect tense is used to describe actions that occurred at an unspecified time in the past or that started in the past and continue to the present.
rules: It is often used with adverbs like 'already', 'yet', 'just', and 'ever'.
examples: The oven is warm and there is a cake on the table. My mother has cooked/baked a cake.
They are standing outside because they don't have their keys. They have lost their keys.
The ground is wet and there are puddles everywhere. It has rained.
commonMistakes: Using Simple Past instead of Present Perfect for unspecified time actions.
Forgetting to use 'has' with third-person singular subjects.

grammar.explanation: 'Been to' is used when someone has visited a place and returned, whereas 'Gone to' is used when someone is still at or on their way to the place.
rules: 'Gone to' implies the person is not back yet.
examples: I know the way to the museum. I have been there many times before.
Where is your sister? She isn't in her room. — She has gone to the supermarket to buy some milk.
commonMistakes: Using 'been to' when the person hasn't returned yet.
Using 'gone to' when the person has already returned.

expressions.meaning: um ao outro, um do outro
expressions.usage: Used to describe reciprocal actions or relationships.
examples: The two companies are in competition with each other.

practiceQuestions.question: Fill in the blanks: I ________ Japan, but I’ve never visited South Korea.
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'Been to' is used because the person has returned from Japan.

practiceQuestions.question: Where is Tom? — No, he ________ the library to study for his finals.
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'Gone to' is used because Tom is still at the library.

culturalNotes: In English-speaking cultures, the Present Perfect is often used to connect past experiences with the present. This can be challenging for speakers of languages that don't have an equivalent tense, like Portuguese.
studyTips: Practice conjugating irregular verbs to master their past participles.
Use timelines to visually connect the Present Perfect with past and present actions.
originalExamples: She spun the globe, and pointed to Latin America. (Ela girou o globo e apontou para a América Latina.)
Light rays bend as they pass from air to water. (Raios de luz se curvam ao passar do ar para a água.)
The two companies are in competition with each other. (As duas empresas estão em competição entre si.)
My grandpa gets very confused sometimes. (Meu avô fica muito confuso às vezes.)
The oven is warm and there is a cake on the table. My mother has cooked/baked a cake. (O forno está quente e há um bolo na mesa. Minha mãe assou um bolo.)
